sentences.text: The genus Maip contains only one known species, M. macrothorax, which is known from an incomplete and disarticulated skeleton.
The known fossil material includes the axis, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, a left coracoid, a fragmentary scapula, a partial right pubis, and a partial metatarsal.
The specific name macrothorax means large chest, referring to the animal's large thoracic cavity.
Maip is estimated to have been around 9 meters long and weighed over 1.3 metric tons.
Maip may represent the largest known megaraptorid from South America and possibly the largest in the world.
Based on ligament attachment traces on the ribs, it is inferred that Maip had a respiratory system comparable to modern birds rather than crocodilians.
The holotype specimen MPM 21545 was discovered by Alexis Rolando in 2019 on the La Anita Farm, 30 km west of El Calafate, Argentina.
The fossil specimen was found disarticulated but associated over an area measuring 5 by 3 square meters.
Maip was first announced in a 2021 preprint but was considered informally named because the paper did not meet necessary requirements.
The genus and species Maip macrothorax were validly described in 2022 by Aranciaga Rolando et al.
Megaraptora is classified within Coelurosauria as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.
Maip is classified within the family Megaraptoridae.
Maip lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in the Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz, Argentina.
Maip lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
